description: Calendar year of the departure date.
Calendar month of the departure date (1–12).
Day within the month (1–31).
Day of the week (1=Monday, 7=Sunday).
Number of distinct trains that departed on this day.
Total individual station stops scheduled across all trains on this day.
Average stops per train (total_schedules_by_day / total_trains_on_route). Higher values indicate longer or more complex routes.
Trains that were fully cancelled at the train level and never ran.
Individual station stops cancelled within otherwise-running trains.
Station stops delayed by at least the configured threshold (DELAY_LONG_DISTANCE_TRAINS minutes).
Fraction of all scheduled stops that were delayed (delay_count_by_day / total_schedules_by_day). Main normalised punctuality metric.
Delayed stops where the stop type is ARRIVAL.
Delayed stops where the stop type is DEPARTURE.
Maximum single delay recorded across all stops on this day (minutes).
Mean delay across all delayed stops on this day (minutes). Only counts stops meeting the threshold.
Median delay across all delayed stops (minutes). More robust to extreme outlier delays than the mean.
Delayed stops with delay in [5, 15) minutes.
Delayed stops with delay in [15, 30) minutes.
Delayed stops with delay in [30, 60) minutes.
Delayed stops with delay >= 60 minutes.
Trains already delayed at their first stop (delay >= threshold at origin). Separates origin-departure issues from en-route accumulation.
mean(differenceInMinutes_eachStation_offset) / mean(differenceInMinutes) over stops with a positive raw delay. >1: delays growing along the route; <1: crews recovering time; ~1: stable.
JSON dict mapping each train type (IC, S, P, …) to the number of its delayed stops on this day.
The 10 most frequently occurring delay values (minutes) across all delayed stops, ordered by frequency.
7-row rolling mean of delay_rate computed over the full sorted history in this file. Smooths day-to-day variability to reveal trends.
